analysis:
The supplied change is a documentation-only edit to docs/developer/build.md. The visible patch excerpt shows a date bump (line 3) and rewrites of the CI runner-routing, job-size and cache sections. Per the file_changes ranges, the head side also changes sections around lines 641-665, 697-719 and 763-769. The excerpt is truncated, so the head text of those sections is not supplied; I reviewed the base text only and did not see the head wording.

The base text describes CI routing (POST /v1/ci/routes to DARKBLOOM_SANDBOX_URL), Blacksmith fallbacks, cache scoping (saves only on master/dev pushes, forks never routed) and the watchdog's limited token permissions. The patch text I can see moves the build jobs, Cluster Release Build Checks and cluster GPU jobs from literal Blacksmith labels to routed lanes with Blacksmith fallback. None of the visible text touches the provider runtime, the coordinator-provider WebSocket, attestation, the encrypted prefix cache (T-041) or the other threat-model assets. No source or executable code changes are visible, so I found no direct regression against the canonical threat model.

Remaining integration questions: the doc rewrite implies workflow changes in provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml and the darkbloom-route workflow. Those files are not in this batch. Routing release-adjacent build jobs through a third-party sandbox plane would matter for build and release trust (A-011, A-017, T-034). The doc still says release, signing and publication keep literal Blacksmith labels. That claim, and whether the build-cluster and build-provider jobs are routed in a way that could affect shipped artifacts, must be verified against the actual workflow diffs, not this doc. Cache-poisoning boundaries (PR-scoped cache entries, master restoring only strict-cache keys) are only described, not changed, in the visible text. I made no deployment or code-level claims.
